messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU queue growth detected for cluster 'eu-west-gpu-primary'. queue_length=+520 (5m), mean_latency=1.9s, active_gpus=48/50, autoscale_attempts=3, autoscale_failures=2. See dashboard: https://redwood.internal/d/cluster/eu-west-gpu-primary
Raj (oncall): I’m paged, looking. Any customer-facing errors?
incident-bot: Amazon SQS consumer backlog + API 429s observed on /v1/generate for some tenants. 5xx rate low. Throttle events rising.
Jen SRE: Paging in. Quick check: recent deploys?
David Eng: I saw a runtime-config push ~12m ago that changed continuous_batching.max_batch_tokens from 2048 -> 4096 and prefix_cache.shards from 8 -> 2 (to save mem). Could be related.
Lisa Ops: Noted — that config was rolled by auto-config-runner at 1939995000.
Raj (oncall): Rolling through metrics now. Is autoscaler hitting max_nodes?
incident-bot: autoscaler: current_replicas=50, max_replicas=50, scale_target=95% util. scale_events: 3 failed due to quota limit (cloud-provider-quotas).
Patrick SRE: So autoscale can't add GPUs; queue grows and batching config may be reducing throughput (batches too big -> increased latency -> pipeline stalls). Possible prefix cache misses after shards cut?
Emily PM: Customer impact: incoming reports from 2 enterprise tenants about high latencies and 429s; CS alerted.
Raj (oncall): Mitigation plan ideas: 1) revert continuous_batching.max_batch_tokens to 2048; 2) revert prefix_cache.shards to 8 so cache hit rate improves; 3) temporarily increase throttle for non-prod/low-tier tenants; 4) open quota request but that's slow. Which is fastest?
David Eng: Reverting batching config is fastest. It's a config flag in our feature-config service. Command: `redwoodctl feature-config set continuous_batching.max_batch_tokens 2048 --env eu-west`
Jen SRE: I'll take the revert and watch queue. Raj, can you apply a temporary per-tenant throttle policy to reduce noisy tenants?
Raj (oncall): On it. Applying policy: `redwoodctl rate-limit add --scope tenant --filter "tier:free" --rps 5 --burst 10 --region eu-west`
incident-bot: ACTION: Raj applied rate-limit for tier=free tenants.
Lisa Ops: Also bumping eviction priority for long-running debug jobs, draining non-critical pools. Command: `k8s-drain --label debug=true --grace 30s --region eu-west`
Patrick SRE: Quick check: prefix cache hit ratio dropped from 92% -> 47% after shard reduction, confirmed by cache metrics. That explains extra backend work.
David Eng: Revert applied: `redwoodctl feature-config set prefix_cache.shards 8 --env eu-west` and `continuous_batching.max_batch_tokens 2048`. Rolling restart of queryrouter nodes to pick up config.
incident-bot: CONFIG-CHANGE: prefix_cache.shards set to 8 by david.eng at 1939995602. continuous_batching.max_batch_tokens set to 2048 by david.eng at 1939995610.
Jen SRE: Observing queue: queue_length dropping from 520 -> 310 in next 2m. Latency trending down: p95 1.9s -> 1.2s.
Emily PM: Noting customers: tenant-abbott and tenant-sparrow reported. CS flagged them and sending incident comms.
Raj (oncall): Still seeing autoscaler failures — we should lift autoscale max to 60 temporarily while cloud quota request is in flight. Any objections?
Patrick SRE: Need to confirm we have spare GPUs; cloud provider quota is the blocker. We can try temporary bursting to partner account. Ops, can you carve additional capacity?
Lisa Ops: We have a partner pool with 12 GPUs in eu-west reserved for bursts. I can remap a subset: `infra-assign --pool partner-burst --to eu-west-gpu-primary --count 8`
David Eng: Assigned +8, cluster now shows capacity 56/58 active. autoscaler should be able to scale.
incident-bot: infra-event: 8 GPUs attached to eu-west-gpu-primary at 1939995800 by lisa.ops.
Raj (oncall): Good. Autoscaler attempt succeeding -> replicas=56. Queue dropping further -> 90.
Jen SRE: p95 now 650ms, p99 1.1s. 429s dropping to near-zero for enterprise tenants.
Emily PM: Emily -> coordinating with CS for a short status update to affected customers: ETA for full recovery?
Raj (oncall): If metrics keep improving, target to mark mitigated in 30m. Will follow up with postmortem.
Patrick SRE: Root cause preliminary: config push reduced prefix_cache shards and increased max_batch_tokens. That decreased cache hit rate and increased per-request token handling which increased locking/queueing in continuous batching runtime. With autoscaler unable to grow (quota), queue surfaced as throttles/latency.
David Eng: Agree. We need immediate fixes + long-term: 1) add a gating test for config changes that touch batching/prefixcache (e.g., a canary that verifies cache hit rate on small canary traffic). 2) Autoscaler should return clearer quota failure alerts and automatic fallback to partner pools. 3) Add rollback runbook for continuous_batching changes.
Lisa Ops: Action items captured in incident board. I'll open infra ticket to request permanent quota increase and document partner pool runbook.
incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated -> status=partial, severity=2, affected_customers=2, mitigation_time=1939995900, incident_channel=incidents. Postmortem owner assigned: Jen SRE.
Jen SRE: I'll own the postmortem. Tagging follow-ups: P0 - quota increase request, P1 - config gating test, P1 - runbook for partner pool failover, P2 - alerts tuning.
Emily PM: I'll coordinate customer comms and include timeline + root cause once we've validated.
Raj (oncall): Handing back to SRE rotation. If anything regresses, page me.
Patrick SRE: Quick note: saved logs of cache metrics and batch timers at /var/logs/incidents/1939999999-cache-batching.log.
David Eng: I'll prepare a small test harness to validate continuous batching param changes in CI.
Jen SRE: Closing the real-time mitigation thread. We'll reconvene for a postmortem meeting at 1940080000 (tomorrow 10:00 UTC).
incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: real-time mitigation flag cleared at 1940001799.
Emily PM: Thanks everyone. Add anything else?
Raj (oncall): thumbs up :thumbsup: great coordination.
Patrick SRE: +1
Lisa Ops: good job team
David Eng: Adding follow-up PR in next 24h
Jen SRE: Logging action items into the incident tracker now.
